description: Ground truth for the deliberately vulnerable cake-shop app. Keep this folder out of the agent's view during evaluation.
line_resolution: Line numbers are not stored. Each entry has an 'anchor' (an exact, unique substring of one line); run tools/check_labels.py to resolve anchors to current line numbers.

vulnerabilities.title: SQL injection in product search
vulnerabilities.notes: User input is built into the query in db.py, two files away from where it enters. Tests cross-file data-flow tracing.

vulnerabilities.title: Server-side template injection in cake-message preview
vulnerabilities.notes: User text is concatenated into the template source itself. Leads to code execution in Jinja2.

vulnerabilities.title: Path traversal in cake image endpoint
vulnerabilities.notes: '../' sequences escape IMAGE_DIR and read any file the process can read, including source code with the secret key.

vulnerabilities.title: Insecure deserialization of cart cookie
vulnerabilities.notes: Attacker controls the cookie, and unpickling it runs arbitrary code.

vulnerabilities.title: Client-controlled price at checkout
vulnerabilities.notes: Price should come from the products table. Any user can buy a cake for 1 UZS.

vulnerabilities.title: Unvalidated quantity allows zero or negative orders
vulnerabilities.notes: The min=1 attribute exists only in the HTML. A negative quantity produces a negative total.

vulnerabilities.title: Stored XSS in product reviews
vulnerabilities.notes: The |safe filter disables Jinja2 autoescaping for user-written review text.

vulnerabilities.title: IDOR: any logged-in user can view any order
vulnerabilities.anchor: order = get_db().execute("SELECT * FROM orders WHERE id = ?", (order_id,)).fetchone()
vulnerabilities.notes: The query is parameterized (no SQLi), but there is no ownership check. Leaks other customers' cake messages and delivery notes. Compare with invoice(), which does check ownership.

vulnerabilities.title: OS command injection in invoice generation
vulnerabilities.notes: The 'format' parameter ends up in a shell command. Requires login and an own order, which an attacker can create.

vulnerabilities.title: Missing authorization on admin order list
vulnerabilities.notes: The other admin routes use @admin_required (defined in auth.py); this one has no decorator at all. Anyone, even logged out, sees all customers' names, emails and addresses.

vulnerabilities.title: Mass assignment lets users make themselves admin
vulnerabilities.source: any extra form field posted to /account
vulnerabilities.notes: The form only shows email and address, but the server accepts is_admin. Subtle: the f-string UPDATE nearby is NOT SQL injection (see D06); the bug is what the allow-list contains.

vulnerabilities.title: Open redirect after login
vulnerabilities.notes: A phishing link can send a customer to an external site right after a real login.

vulnerabilities.title: Hardcoded, guessable session secret key
vulnerabilities.notes: Anyone who knows or guesses the key can forge Flask session cookies, e.g. session['user_id'] = 1 (admin).

vulnerabilities.title: Flask debug mode enabled
vulnerabilities.notes: The Werkzeug debugger allows code execution if reachable. Bound to localhost here, so severity depends on deployment context.

vulnerabilities.title: Passwords hashed with unsalted MD5
vulnerabilities.notes: Fast, unsalted hash. Combined with V01, leaked hashes crack instantly.

vulnerabilities.title: Vulnerable Flask version
vulnerabilities.notes: Expected to be reported by pip-audit (e.g. CVE-2023-30861).

vulnerabilities.title: Vulnerable Werkzeug version
vulnerabilities.notes: Expected to be reported by pip-audit (e.g. CVE-2024-34069, debugger-related, which interacts with V14).

vulnerabilities.title: Vulnerable Jinja2 version
vulnerabilities.notes: Expected to be reported by pip-audit (several 2024 Jinja2 CVEs).

vulnerabilities.title: No CSRF protection on any state-changing form
vulnerabilities.notes: App-wide missing control with no single line to point at. Count as found if the report flags missing CSRF protection anywhere.

decoys.title: f-string SQL with an allow-listed table name
decoys.why_safe: count_rows() rejects any table not in ALLOWED_TABLES, and callers pass constants.

decoys.title: subprocess with a fixed argument list
decoys.why_safe: No shell, no user input in the arguments.

decoys.title: render_template_string with a constant template
decoys.why_safe: User input is passed as a context variable and autoescaped, not concatenated into the template source.

decoys.title: File serving with secure_filename and send_from_directory
decoys.why_safe: secure_filename strips path components, and send_from_directory refuses paths outside the directory.

decoys.title: Admin stats route
decoys.why_safe: Protected by @admin_required, defined in auth.py. Verifying this needs a cross-file lookup.

decoys.title: f-string UPDATE with an allow-listed column name
decoys.why_safe: Column names are checked against USER_COLUMNS and values are parameterized, so it is not SQL injection. (The allow-list content is a separate bug, V11.)

decoys.title: Invoice lookup with ownership check
decoys.anchor: "SELECT * FROM orders WHERE id = ? AND user_id = ?"
decoys.why_safe: The query is restricted to the current user's orders.

decoys.title: Search term reflected in results page
decoys.why_safe: Jinja2 autoescaping is on for .html templates and no |safe is used.
